 Hon'Ble Anish Kumar Gupta, J. 
1. Heard Sri Lavkush Kumar, Advocate holding brief of Sri Uma Dutt Shukla, , learned counsel for
the applicants, Sri Pradeep Kumar Tiwari, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and Ms.
Harshita Rani, learned Aga for the State.

2.  The instant application has been filed by applicants seeking quashing of the charge-sheet dated 18.02.2024 and the cognizance/summoning order dated 08.01.2025 as well as entire proceeding of Case No.379 of 2025 (State of U.P. vs Irfan and another) arising out of Case Crime No.351 of 2023 under Sections 498A, 323 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Dowry prohibition Act, Police Station Etmadpur,
District Agra, pending before the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.4 Agra.
3.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.4 Agra
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant submits that there was a matrimonial discord between the applicant no.1 and the opposite party no.3, due to which the instant FIR was lodged by the opposite party no.2 (father of opposite party no.3) against the applicants herein.

However, during the proceeding of the instant case before the trial court, the parties have settled their dispute amicably and a compromise dated 20.02.2025 was executed between the parties, copy of which has been annexed as annexure 3 to the instant application.

Vide order dated 19.09.2025, the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court had directed the parties to appear before the trial court for verification of compromise and in terms of the said order, the parties appeared before the trial court on 27.10.2025.
In presence of the parties, the trial court verified the compromise.

Certified copy of the compromise along with the order verifying the compromise has been annexed to the short counter affidavit filed by learned counsel for the opposite party no.2, which is taken on record.

4. Learned counsel for the applicants as well as learned counsel for opposite party no.2 have jointly prayed for quashing of the entire proceeding of the instant case in terms of the compromise which has been duly verified by the trial court.
Learned AGA also does not oppose the prayer for quashing of the entire proceeding of the instant case.
5. Having heard the rival submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court has carefully gone through the record of the case.

From the record of the case, it is apparent that the entire dispute between the parties had arisen due to matrimonial discord between the applicant and the opposite party no.2, who are the husband and wife respectively and the parties have settled all their disputes amicably.

With the aforesaid settlement, the peace will prevail in the in the family as well as in the society and continuance of the aforesaid criminal proceedings will not serve any fruitful purpose in view of the settlement of disputes between parties.

In view of the aforesaid facts and in the light of the judgments of the Apex Court in Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab,
(2014) 6 SCC 466 : Prabatbhai Aahir Alias Prabatbhai Bhimsinghbhai Karmur and others vs. State of Gujarat and Another , (2017) 9 SCC 641 and Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and Another, (2012)
10 SCC 303, the instant application deserves to be allowed.
